mapping.azimuth: houses west to east by longitude, sector angle proportional to 2 + people (4 degree gaps), the eldest founder's house (Etruria / Maer) at azimuth 0 (+Z)
mapping.dye: the contract's dye colours, stepped by generations of descent from the founders: step k = round(-log2(share)), 0 to 4, drawn as the tapestry's colour at the equivalent share 1 - k/8 (deeper = closer; 1/16 or less is floored at the tapestry's 1/2 colour); a share of 0 (no descent in the data, in-laws) is ecru
mapping.elevation: layout only: inside a house, depth-first order of descent (children by birth, in-laws beside their spouse) from top to bottom
mapping.fiber: a life runs radially from r(born) to r(died); a spawn arc on the birth shell joins it to a parent; a move bends it along the shell of the move year (dotted when the year is not in the data); a death not in the data is dashed after the last dated event, to the tapestry's 60-year end
mapping.focus: on a close shot (CU, MCU) or a pick the subject's threads burn brightest, the line back to the founders stays lit (at most 32 people: the main line by the larger share of descent, the other parent at each step, then other ancestors) and every other thread dims to a fifth; a bead marks the stop's event, ringed when it is a marriage (drawn at the middle of the arc)
lines: Radius = time: 1725 at the core, 2000 at the glass, 286.5 years per pocket unit, shells every 50 years. Azimuth: houses west to east, angle = 2 + people. Elevation: order of descent (layout only).
Each life a fiber, each marriage an arc on the shell of its year.
mapping.marriage: an arc on the shell of the wedding year between the spouses' fibers; a close marriage (phi > 0) is doubled and brighter in the dye; an estimated year is dashed and translucent
mapping.nesting: the pocket sits in its host at scale 6: 1 pocket unit = 6 host units; a century = 2.09 host units
mapping.radius: r(year) = 0.08 + (year - 1725) x 0.003491 pocket units: 1725 at the seed edge, 2000 at r 1.04 just inside the glass (r 1.1); 286.5 years per pocket unit; time shells every 50 years from 1750
mapping.root: a founder's root line from the seed to their birth point is layout only (no years of life)
mapping.short: Radius = time: 1725 at the core, 2000 at the glass, 286.5 years per pocket unit, shells every 50 years. Azimuth: houses west to east, angle = 2 + people. Elevation: order of descent (layout only).

computed.text: 76 lives and 12 marriages (3 between close kin), in 8 houses placed west to east: Shrewsbury (The Mount), Etruria / Maer, Barlaston, Erasmus Darwin's household, Leith Hill Place, Hensleigh Wedgwood's household, Down House, Cambridge.
green = Darwin, blue = Wedgwood descent (deeper = closer); warm grey = neither; dashed = an estimated year.

narration.text: A sphere of time: the founders sit at the centre (1725), the present is the glass (2000). Each life is a fiber running outward from birth to death; each marriage is an arc on the shell of its year.

computed.text: Founders of the dyes: darwin (#2f6b3a): Erasmus Darwin 1731–1802 and Mary Howard 1740–1770; wedgwood (#3f74a8): Josiah Wedgwood 1730–1795 and Sarah Wedgwood 1734–1815.
22 children of the founders are in the file, born 1758–1790.

The first moves between houses: Robert from Erasmus Darwin's household to Shrewsbury (The Mount), on the 1797? marriage (both spouses cross); Susannah from Etruria / Maer to Shrewsbury (The Mount), on the 1797? marriage (both spouses cross); Francis from Etruria / Maer to Barlaston (year not in the data: drawn dotted); Hensleigh from Etruria / Maer to Hensleigh Wedgwood's household, on the 1828? marriage; Charles from Shrewsbury (The Mount) to Down House, on the 1838? marriage (both spouses cross); Emma from Etruria / Maer to Down House, on the 1838? marriage (both spouses cross).
A move rides the wedding arc when the spouse was already in that house; a dotted move has no year in the data.
The 1838 marriage (year estimated: not in the data): Charles Darwin and Emma Darwin (née Wedgwood), first cousins, kinship φ = 1/16, drawn doubled.
Their 10 children in the file carry the dyes darwin 1/4; wedgwood 1/2.
3 of the 12 marriages in this file are close (the couple share founders in the data), 1829–1842; each is drawn doubled. 3 of those years are not in the data and are drawn at an estimate (marked ?).
Fibers that cross on a close marriage: 2 brides, 2 grooms.

The file has no closing dates. Its "closed" year per house is the last death among the house's core members: Shrewsbury (The Mount) 1881; Etruria / Maer 1885; Hensleigh Wedgwood's household 1891; Erasmus Darwin's household 1911; Down House 1943; Barlaston 1956; Leith Hill Place 1958; Cambridge 1989.
Where that differs from a narrated closing, the data list (data-issues.json) records it; the sphere does not.
